Appearance:
Shri Abhishek Gilke - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the responden
 Order
1 . It is seen from the record that though owner and driver both have been served, but they have not entered appearance.
2. With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is finally heard.

3. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant / claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 1/5/2015 passed in MACC No.207/2011 by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.1,16,300/- has been awarded to the appellant / claimant by way of compensation.
4 . Short facts of the case are that on 2/5/2011 in the evening at 5.30 PM appellant Radhabai along with her sister and daughter were going for attending a marriage ceremony at Indore.

When they were on their way, respondent No.3, the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24728 2 MA-1488-2015 No.M.P. 09 - S - 9834 owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.1 driving in rash and negligent manner, dashed the said bus upon appellant - Radhabai because of which she sustained several injuries on various parts of her body as well as suffered fracture in clavicle bone and pelvic bone, she was admitted in the hospital for treatment.
5 . Thereafter the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to her on account of the injuries sustained to her.
The application was contested by respondent No.1 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the Smt. Radha Bai vs United Insurance Co. Ltd. on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192245801/
1 evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,16,300/-.
6 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Dr. Dinesh Gupta (PW.2) has stated in his evidence before the tribunal that the appellant has suffered 22% permanent disability into her pelvic bone and shoulder for which permanent disability certificate Exhibit P/56 was produced before the claims tribunal.

The claims tribunal after considering the certificate has considered this permanent disability only to the extent of 7.5% with respect to over all body which in the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant should have taken at least at 11%.
He further submits that for the injuries in the accident she has to remained under treatment for a long period.
She remained hospitalized for a period of 5 days.
Looking to the nature of injuries and period of hospitalization as well as duration of treatment the amount of Rs.2000/- awarded by the claims tribunal for pain and suffering is very less.
Thus he prays for enhancement of the amount of compensation.

As NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24728 3 MA-1488-2015 regards the liability of the Insurance Company the learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claims tribunal though found that the vehicle was being plied in breach of Insurance policy but it was a matter between the owner and insurer of the vehicle for which the claimant should not be made to suffer.
The claims tribunal has incorrectly held in para 26 of the award that the direction for pay and recover can only be made by the Hon'ble Apex Court and no such power lies with the claims tribunal.

He submits that it has now already been settled by various pronouncement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as by this Court where in such cases where the breach of only about license of permit of the vehicle then pay and recover can be directed.
In support of his contention he placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shamanna V/s.
Divisional Manager The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. reported as (2018) ACJ 2163 , Pepsu Road Transport Corporation V/s. National Insurance Co. reported as (2013) ACJ 2440 and Ram Milan Yadav & Ors.

entities.text: Pepsu Road Transport Corporation V/s. National Insurance Co. reported as (2013) ACJ 2440
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: V/s. Ramji @ Ramjisharan Pal & Ors . dated 28/7/2025 passed in M.A.No.4031/2018.
7 . Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1 / Insurance Co. submits that the nature of injuries to the appellant was not grievous.
She had only remained hospitalized for a limited period of 5 days.
Looking to the same the amount of Rs.1,16,300/- as awarded by the claims tribunal is reasonable and no interference is warranted in this regard.
As regards the liability of the Insurance Company he submits that not only that the driver of the vehicle was not having a valid license but even the permit of the bus was not available.
As such the vehicle was being plied in complete breach of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24728 4 MA-1488-2015 insurance policy.
As such the claims tribunal has correctly exonerated Insurance Company from liability of payment of compensation.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. From the perusal of the record, it is clear that the claims tribunal has accepted the permanent disability certificate Exhibit P/56, which certifies the permanent disability of the appellant at 22%
into her pelvic bone and left shoulder.
Apart from this appellant has suffered several other injuries for which the amount of Rs.2000/- under the head of pain and suffering appears to be very less.

2 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the question of payment of compensation, the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant is right in contending that the conclusion of the claims tribunal in para 26 is not sustainable in the eyes of law.
The claims tribunal can always award pay and recover in appropriate cases.
In the present case as the breach was of driving license and the permit thus it is not the case of no claim, no insurance.

Insurance of the vehicle is very much there and the breach of policy is a matter between the owner of the vehicle and the insurer for which the claimant who has suffered the agony in accident should not be made to suffer.
The case law as relied by the learned counsel for the appellant clearly holds the same.

11. In the light of the above discussion and the law as laid down by the Apex Court as well as this Court, it is directed that the Insurance Company shall first pay the compensation to the claimant and then it may recover the same from the owner / driver of the vehicle.

12. As regards the quantum of compensation in view of the above NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24728 5 MA-1488-2015 analysis, this Court is of the considered view that if another in lumpsum amount of Rs.40,000/- is paid to the appellant, then it will constitute a just and proper compensation in the facts of the present case.
It is hence directed that the appellant be paid Rs.40,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount of Rs.40,000/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
13. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands allowed in part and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
